premise: A plotter exploration forked from the daily archive piece 'Overstruck' (Day 147). The daily track asks what a Noah source reduces to in the engine's own vocabulary; this strand asks what the line-printer piece becomes when a PEN — not a screen — makes its marks. The parent's canonical raster is never altered. Everything here is either a faithful translation of that parent to pen (a rendition) or a study that deliberately leaves it behind.

forkRule.line: Fidelity. A plot is a faithful EXPORT while it still reproduces the parent's checksum; it becomes a STUDY the moment a decision changes what is DRAWN, not just how it is output.
forkTriggers: a different glyph vocabulary, or a re-seeded / re-composed layout
tone remapped to exploit ink/pen behaviour (would no longer match the raster)
multi-pen / colour separation — more than one pen layer with intent
an engine capability built for pen aesthetics rather than to reduce a Noah source
a series: a 2nd/3rd variation kept as an artwork in its own right
forkRule.tell: When the pen stops reproducing the piece and starts making decisions the screen never made.

Solid-fill pitch calibration strip (0.40 / 0.45 / 0.50 / 0.55 / 0.60 mm) for the 0.5 mm pen. Pick the widest pitch that still reads solid on paper, then re-export the parent at that pitch.
